summary: S. 1378 directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to enhance its use of artificial intelligence for weather, water, wildfire, and space weather forecasting. It mandates the creation of training datasets, the exploration of global and regional artificial intelligence weather models, technical assistance for emergency managers and forecasters, and public-private partnerships while protecting national security interests.

affected_groups.effect: Tasks the agency with developing artificial intelligence weather models, training datasets, public data access plans, reports to Congress, and retaining expert personnel.
Receives technical assistance, data access, and support to test and evaluate artificial intelligence weather models and best practices.
Receives support to make operational decisions based on combined outputs from artificial intelligence and numerical weather models.
Aims to improve readiness, preparedness, risk mitigation, and safety through advanced artificial intelligence applications.
affected_groups.group: Firefighters and Communities at Risk from Wildfires

key_provisions: Requires the Under Secretary to develop and curate comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets within four years, building on existing federal datasets.
Authorizes the development, testing, and experimentation of global, regional, and local artificial intelligence weather models.
Requires technical assistance, data access, and support for forecasters, scientists, and emergency managers to evaluate artificial intelligence models and make operational decisions.
Authorizes novel public-private, academic, and international partnership and co-investment strategies for research and development.

Directs the creation of a plan to make operational and experimental artificial intelligence weather models, documentation, and related data available to the public at no cost, subject to national security and privacy protections.
Requires a report to Congress regarding national security and economic risks from foreign countries of concern accessing U.S. weather data.
Authorizes appropriations of $105,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 and $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030.
missing_information: Specific details on internal agency reorganization or exact personnel salary caps.
Definitive long-term appropriations beyond fiscal year 2030.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 1378 directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to enhance its use of artificial intelligence for weather, water, wildfire, and space weather forecasting. It mandates the creation of training datasets, the exploration of global and regional artificial intelligence weather models, technical assistance for emergency managers and forecasters, and public-private partnerships while protecting national security interests.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs federal modernization of weather forecasting through artificial intelligence, authorizing up to $105 million in fiscal year 2026 and $25 million annually from 2027 through 2030 for NOAA to expand machine learning and data-sharing capabilities.
